slot_note: redraw, second new cell this round: the ambulance surge pool (v1, never carded) and the macro-econometrics cell are spent without a card; see the design note's Tried and rejected
niche: a medical humanitarian organisation running two treatment centres in the fictional Marrisford Province projecting December's Tamberlow virus disease cases under the provincial response plan's central scenario, from the outbreak's own line list and transmission links
analyst_test: A strong analyst who dedups the line list, fits the serial interval to every source-to-case pair in the transmission links (11 days), takes the reproduction number from the six weeks' growth (1.5), halves it from 2 November and runs the renewal equation forward files about 4,000 cases for weeks 49 to 52 against 5,000, because the tracing system holds a link only once its case has fallen ill, so September's and October's sources appear only with the cases they infected quickly.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the outbreak's generation interval estimated from transmission pairs that are right-truncated at the extract while incidence grows, which is how infectious-disease modellers turn a growth rate into a reproduction number and project under a control scenario; swap in hospital admissions or shipments and there is no chain of who infected whom, no interval between linked onsets and no renewal equation, so the task stops reading.
layer1: mixed date formats between field forms and laboratory-fed rows
a case notified in two districts under two case numbers with one laboratory sample
notified people later found not to be cases left in the line list with their final classification
transmission links entered with a certainty grade and links whose case was later discarded
a weekly situation report counting by notification week, not onset week
stakeholder_role: the organisation's medical planning lead for the Marrisford response

spine.entity: one notified suspected, probable or confirmed case

world.org_type: international medical humanitarian organisation running treatment centres

driver: An interval between two linked events, read from the pairs a record holds at its cut-off, is shorter than the interval the process runs on while the process is growing, because a pair enters the record only once its later event has happened and the pairs still open at the cut-off are the long ones from the recent and most numerous earlier events; the reproduction number taken from the growth rate on the record's interval is too low, so a projection under a planned cut in transmission falls away too fast.
driver_concrete: Each source-to-case link enters the tracing system only when the infected contact falls ill and is notified, so at the 18 October extract the cases of September and October are listed only with the contacts they infected quickly; the serial interval read off the links is shorter than the one the chains run on once each pair is read against the time its source had to the cut-off, the reproduction number from the six weeks' growth comes out too low, and the projection under the plan's halving of transmission shows weeks 49 to 52 about a quarter lower than they will be.
stump: A competent analyst fits the serial interval to every source-to-case pair in the transmission links, takes the reproduction number from the growth of onsets over epidemiological weeks 36 to 41, halves it from 2 November and projects about 4,000 cases for weeks 49 to 52 instead of about 5,000, because the tracing system holds a link only once its case has fallen ill.

differentiation.task98: task98 v6 counts units leaving a score class by an improvement step read from treated and untreated twins in a flow model; here nothing crosses a threshold, the decisive quantity is a delay distribution read from linked pairs that the extract truncates while incidence grows, and it enters through a renewal equation
differentiation.task468: task468 v2 and v3 apply cost and persistence by each active unit's own time since start or since its current spell; here no unit's duration conditions its outcome, the record's pairs are a growth-weighted, right-truncated sample of one transmission interval, corrected by reading each pair against the time its source had at the cut-off
differentiation.task126: task126 splits units joined by a succession link that a certifying corpus blesses; here no units are joined or split, and the decisive step is a delay distribution corrected for right truncation at the extract
differentiation.task138: task138 rebuilds each unit's store at the forecast date from its inputs at the share that reaches the store, identified from monitored units; here there is no store or balance, the record's linked pairs are a truncated sample of one interval and the correction reads each pair against its source's time to the cut-off
differentiation.task82: task82 attributes one-off keyed records to holders through a second system's ledger and a transaction reference; here nothing is attributed or joined across systems, and the step is estimating an interval distribution under truncation
differentiation.task133: task133 enters each taken-over loan only from the takeover (left truncation of exposure time in a life table); here the truncation is on the right and by the later of two linked events, and the estimated quantity is a delay distribution feeding a renewal equation, not an outcome rate by age
differentiation.task196: task196 recovers how many events happened from the overlap of two capture channels; here nothing is uncounted, every case is in the line list, and the record's links are a growth-weighted, right-truncated sample of one interval
differentiation.task180: task180 completes small events masked by a daily noise cycle at the instruments; here the missing records are the long intervals whose later event has not yet happened at the extract, corrected by conditioning each pair on its source's time to the cut-off
